article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 65% Indica / 35% Sativa
Genetics: Orange Skunk × White Widow
Breeder: De Sjamaan Cannabis Seeds
THC Content: 24%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet fruit, citrus, Skunk, earth, spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): 7–8.5 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: 100 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Moderated
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

The Magician reaches back to a period of cannabis breeding when Skunk and White Widow genetics dominated Dutch seed catalogs and flavor descriptions revolved around fruit, spice, resin, and unmistakable marijuana funk rather than pastries and candy. De Sjamaan created the cultivar by crossing Orange Skunk with White Widow, deliberately aiming to recreate some of the livelier character associated with early Skunk hybrids . The breeder describes a substantial plant carrying long, solid flowers coated in visible resin, with a strong fruity aroma and an upbeat high. Although its genetic percentages technically place it on the indica side, the finished experience is broader than that classification suggests, combining physical relaxation with clear, energetic, and euphoric mental effects.
Genetics and Lineage

The official lineage of The Magician is Orange Skunk × White Widow. De Sjamaan presents the cultivar as a return to older Skunk breeding, noting that early Skunks drew from Afghan, Mexican, and Colombian cannabis before later breeding increasingly emphasized the Afghan side. Orange Skunk supplies the sweet, pungent Skunk foundation, while White Widow contributes resin coverage, potency, and a more complex cerebral dimension.

White Widow is one of the landmark Dutch marijuana cultivars of the 1990s and is closely associated with breeder Ingemar, whose work is also connected with De Sjamaan. Its reputation was built around unusually resinous flowers and balanced effects rather than a single extreme trait. Combined with Orange Skunk, that genetic background gives The Magician both classic Skunk vigor and the crystal-heavy flower structure that made Widow genetics so influential.

The pairing is considerably simpler than the multigenerational polyhybrids common today. Rather than stacking several dessert, fuel, and Cookies descendants into one pedigree, The Magician joins two recognizable old-school families. That straightforward ancestry is central to the cultivar’s personality: pungent cannabis aroma, substantial branching, resin-coated buds, and a high that moves between cerebral energy and physical comfort.
Effects and Experience

The effect begins more brightly than the 65% indica classification might imply. De Sjamaan describes The Magician as energetic, happy, euphoric, clear, inspiring, and motivating while also acknowledging a physical component. That mixture creates an experience with two distinct layers rather than the immediate heaviness often associated with indica-dominant weed.

During the early portion of the high, mood can rise and ordinary activities may feel more engaging. Conversation, music, creative work, or relaxed social settings fit naturally with this phase because the mental effect remains relatively clear rather than overwhelmingly dreamy. White Widow’s influence is especially apparent here, adding an expansive quality that keeps the cultivar from behaving like a purely sedating Skunk.

As the experience develops, the heavier side becomes more noticeable. Muscular tension may ease and the pace of activity can slow, although the mental component generally remains present. Dose matters considerably. The breeder no longer provides a laboratory THC percentage, so contemporary flower should be judged by its own test results rather than an assumed number. Larger amounts can also turn an otherwise upbeat experience into stronger intoxication, with possible dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, or impaired coordination.
Medical Benefits

The Magician has not been evaluated as an individual cultivar in controlled clinical trials, so the strain itself cannot be considered a proven treatment for pain, anxiety, insomnia, depression, or another medical condition. Its potential relevance to medical marijuana comes from its cannabinoids and the broader evidence surrounding cannabis rather than from the name or pedigree.

Research summarized by the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health indicates that cannabis and cannabinoids may provide modest benefit for certain types of chronic pain. Specific cannabinoid medications also have established roles in treating chemotherapy-associated nausea and vomiting, while research into sleep and other symptoms remains more variable.

The cultivar’s combination of mental uplift and later physical relaxation may appeal to patients who do not want an immediately sedating experience. At the same time, THC-rich cannabis can impair attention and coordination and may provoke anxiety or dizziness in susceptible people. Medical consumers should therefore place greater weight on laboratory testing of the actual product and personal response than on generalized strain descriptions .
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The Magician belongs firmly to the traditional Skunk-and-fruit school of cannabis flavor. De Sjamaan describes the taste as strong and sweet, while its historical breeder description emphasizes a pronounced fruity fragrance. Beneath that sweetness lies a deeper Skunk character—earthy, pungent, slightly musky, and distinctly herbal.

The Orange Skunk side can contribute a brighter citrus impression, particularly when fresh flowers are broken apart. That quality does not necessarily resemble modern orange candy strains; it is more likely to present as citrus peel layered into sweet fruit and cannabis funk. White Widow adds additional earthy and spicy depth, allowing the finish to become drier and more herbal after the sweeter opening fades.

No authoritative terpene analysis is published for the cultivar, so exact dominant compounds should not be assigned without laboratory data from a specific batch. Growing environment, harvest maturity, drying temperature, and curing can all alter the final aromatic balance. The breeder-supported description is therefore the most reliable one: strong, sweet, fruity cannabis with a pungent old-school foundation.
Growing Information

The Magician develops into a considerably larger plant than many compact modern indica hybrids. De Sjamaan lists indoor height at approximately 120–200 centimeters and outdoor plants at roughly 200–300 centimeters. Long, solid flower formations develop along the branches, and the finished buds can become heavily coated with resin.

Indoor flowering requires approximately 7–8.5 weeks, putting the cultivar in a manageable range despite its relatively tall structure. Growers working in limited vertical space should account for stretch before flowering is advanced. An even canopy can help prevent the tallest branches from taking excessive light while lower sites remain shaded. The combination of Skunk vigor and White Widow flower production also means branches can require support as flowers gain mass.

Outdoors, De Sjamaan places harvest around the end of October, with mature plants potentially reaching two to three meters. That relatively late finish favors locations where autumn conditions remain stable enough for flowers to mature without prolonged cold or excessive moisture. Good airflow around the long buds becomes particularly important as resin production and flower density increase.

Historical breeder material reproduced in older catalogs placed indoor yield around 100 grams per square meter, although the current De Sjamaan listing does not publish a yield specification. Because that historical number is unusually modest by modern standards, it is better treated as an archival breeder reference than a universal expectation. Lighting, plant count, vegetative time, training, container size, and phenotype will have a major effect on actual production.
FAQ
What are the genetics of The Magician?
The Magician was bred by De Sjamaan Cannabis Seeds from Orange Skunk crossed with White Widow. The breeder lists the resulting cultivar as 65% indica and 35% sativa.
Is The Magician indica or sativa?

It is officially an indica-dominant hybrid at 65% indica and 35% sativa. Despite that ratio, De Sjamaan describes the effects as clear, energetic, euphoric, inspiring, and physically noticeable rather than purely sedating.
What does The Magician strain taste like?

Its flavor is primarily sweet and fruity with citrus, earthy Skunk, herbal, and spicy undertones. The Orange Skunk parent supplies much of the sweeter pungency, while White Widow adds additional depth.
How long does The Magician take to flower?
De Sjamaan lists an indoor flowering period of approximately 7–8.5 weeks. Outdoors, the cultivar typically reaches maturity near the end of October in the Northern Hemisphere.
How tall does The Magician grow?

Indoor plants generally reach about 120–200 centimeters according to the breeder. Outdoor specimens can become substantially larger, with De Sjamaan listing approximately 200–300 centimeters under suitable conditions.
Final Thoughts on The Magician

The Magician is best understood as a deliberate return to classic Dutch cannabis breeding. Its Orange Skunk × White Widow pedigree connects two influential genetic traditions without burying them beneath multiple generations of newer hybrids . Sweet fruit and citrus meet pungent Skunk, spice, earth, and heavy resin, creating a profile that feels unmistakably different from today’s abundance of Cookies, Gelato, Runtz, and dessert-derived marijuana.

Its effects are equally characteristic of that older approach. Although indica dominates the genetic ratio, the experience maintains enough mental energy to remain uplifting, creative, and engaging before physical relaxation becomes more noticeable. This balance gives The Magician more versatility than its classification alone suggests.

For growers and consumers interested in classic European weed genetics, the strain offers a direct link to the era when Skunk and White Widow defined much of the premium seed market. Its considerable height, quick-to-moderate flowering period, resinous flowers, and sweet pungent aroma make it more than a nostalgic cultivar. The Magician preserves a recognizable old-school cannabis personality that has become increasingly uncommon as modern breeding has moved toward much more complex genetic combinations.
